t.8.2: Bondage is when the mind desires something or grieves over something, gives up something or takes hold of something, is delighted by something or is angered by something.
t.8.3: Liberation is when the mind does not desire, does not grieve, does not reject, does not grasp, does not rejoice, and does not become angry.
t.8.4: There is bondage when the mind is attached to any views at all; there is liberation when the mind is unattached to all views.
t.8.5: When there is no "I," then there is liberation; when there is "I," then there is bondage. Knowing this, effortlessly, as if in play, neither grasp nor let go of anything.
